correctness.rationale: Connected bipartite Hall description yields affine space ∑A x=∑B y and all box inequalities plus the one nonredundant Hall x(A0)≤y(B1). Orthogonal projection of ambient normals to this (2n−1)-space gives ell_n=√((2n−1)/(2n)) for a coordinate and sqrt(n/2) for Hall. Hence upper bounds r≤1/(2ell), r≤(n−s)/(n ell+sqrt(n/2)). Centers 1/2 in the box regime, or r ell on A0∪B0 and 1−r ell on A1∪B1 in Hall regime, achieve equality; saturated bounds plus affine equality force uniqueness. Equality of radii would require n−2s=n/√(2n−1), impossible for integers by irrationality/divisibility. Facet classification uses Mori Prop.3.4; independently LP-checked all n=2..4,s=1..n−1 using true projected normal lengths. Finite tests are not the all-n proof.
